public_safe_summary: AI Film directing must actually run the overall canonical director system rather than only imitate the output that such a system would be expected to produce.
desired_effect: Ordinary AI Film directing should truly traverse the applicable canonical directing workflow, with enough mechanism-backed evidence to distinguish real system execution from an answer that merely resembles one.
problem_to_solve: The owner-domain canonical already defines mandatory directing reads, compiler, route scan and learning gates, while the shared Second Brain defines a RuntimeInvocationReceipt contract; the remaining gap is to make claimed full-system directing execution mechanically verifiable in the owner-domain path.
success_condition: A normal AI Film directing invocation can prove the applicable canonical entry, mandatory reads, routes and capabilities were actually resolved; missing mechanism evidence cannot be reported as a verified full-system run, and routine directing does not become durable planning backlog merely because it executed.
risks: A plausible directing answer may be mistaken for real system execution when actual read, route and capability evidence is absent.
assumptions: The current AI Film repository remains the owner-domain authority for directing behavior.
unknowns: Whether any non-repository execution instrumentation already exists outside the current owner canonical is UNKNOWN.
dependencies: Any owner-domain implementation change needed to satisfy this requirement requires a separately governed AI Film task and write authority.
